papers.title: Heat-Inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Intestinal Barrier Function.
papers.abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, progressive, immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract. Methods: This study used C57BL/6J mice induced by DSS to construct an intestinal inflammation model, and explored the alleviating effect and potential mechanism of heat inactivated Lactobacillus paracasei PC-01 (PC-01) on intestinal inflammation. Results: The results showed that heat-inactivated PC-01 significantly decreased the Disease Activity Index and H&E histopathological scores (p < 0.05). It also reduced the serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokin
papers.summary: In a DSS-induced mouse model of colitis, heat-inactivated Lacticaseibacillus paracasei PC-01 reduced disease activity and histopathological damage and lowered serum pro-inflammatory cytokines. The protective effect appears to be mediated through modulation of the gut microbiota and improvement of intestinal barrier function.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of developmental-category-associated fungal communities in the gut contents of Achatina fulica, an intermediate host of Angiostrongylus cantonensis.
papers.abstract: The invasive giant African snail (Achatina fulica) poses serious agricultural and ecological threats and serves as an important intermediate host of the zoonotic parasite Angiostrongylus cantonensis, which causes human eosinophilic meningitis. While its gut bacterial microbiome has been extensively characterized, the gut mycobiome remains largely uncharacterized. In particular, variations in gut fungal communities across developmental stages remain unknown, limiting our understanding of the A. fulica gut holobiont.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the fungal communities (mycobiome) in the gut contents of the giant African snail Achatina fulica, an invasive species and intermediate host for the parasite that causes human eosinophilic meningitis. The authors compare fungal community composition across different developmental stages of the snail, addressing a gap since the gut bacterial microbiome had been studied but the mycobiome was largely unknown. The work provides a baseline description of developmental-stage-associated fungal diversity in this host.

papers.title: Bacterial community profiles of soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve, Philippines.
papers.abstract: The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve harbors diverse microorganisms with potential biotechnological applications, yet bacterial taxonomic profiling across its watersheds remains limited. Amplicon metagenome sequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene revealed Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as dominant phyla, with Actinobacteriota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexi, Myxococcota, Methylomirabilota, Bacteroidota, Nitrospirota, and Planctomycetota present at varying abundances.
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to profile bacterial communities in soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve in the Philippines. Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota were the dominant phyla, with ten additional phyla present at varying abundances across watersheds. The work provides a baseline taxonomic survey of an understudied tropical forest soil environment.

papers.title: Functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover across coral-associated microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coral-associated microbiomes are fundamental to holobiont health and resilience, yet their community structures often demonstrate high taxonomic variability across host species. Whether such variability results in functional instability or reflects pervasive metabolic redundancy remains unclear. Here, we investigated microbial taxonomic structure, functional potential, and community assembly mechanisms across 15 coral species using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. These communities exhibited extreme taxonomic heterogeneity, high beta-diversity, and the absence of a universall
papers.summary: Across 15 coral species, microbial communities showed extreme taxonomic variability but maintained similar functional potential, indicating metabolic redundancy and functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover. The study used 16S rRNA sequencing and shotgun metagenomics to show that high beta-diversity does not translate into functional instability.

papers.title: Exploratory associations of gut microbiota composition with HBeAg and HBsAg status in nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B.
papers.abstract: HBeAg and HBsAg reflect viral replication and host immune status and are important determinants of treatment responsiveness in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The gut microbiota, a key component of the gut-liver axis, may influence immune regulation and antiviral outcomes. This study characterized gut microbiota profiles across different HBeAg and HBsAg statuses in CHB patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy. Fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 29 healthy controls (HC) and 101 NA-treated CHB patients without cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma, including 30 HBeAg-po
papers.summary: This study used fecal shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare gut microbiota profiles in 101 nucleos(t)ide analog-treated chronic hepatitis B patients (stratified by HBeAg and HBsAg status) and 29 healthy controls. The authors characterized microbial compositional differences associated with serological status, suggesting the gut microbiota may relate to immune regulation and antiviral treatment response in CHB. As an exploratory, cross-sectional analysis, the findings are associative and require validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

papers.title: Exploring antimicrobial resistance in wild and domestic animal populations: combining publicly available data with BV-BRC resources to introduce bioinformatics in an undergraduate classroom.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatics blends the fields of biology, statistics, computer science, and information technology for the processing and analysis of genomic data. Despite the growing demand for trained bioinformaticians and a positive job market outlook, most undergraduate institutions struggle to integrate bioinformatics into their life science curricula. Educators face numerous barriers to incorporating bioinformatics into their classes, including technical issues and expertise. To address this need, we are developing web-accessible, course-based materials for general microbiology, infectious disease, g
papers.summary: This paper describes the development of web-accessible, course-based bioinformatics materials for undergraduate microbiology and infectious disease classes, using antimicrobial resistance data from wild and domestic animal populations combined with BV-BRC (Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center) resources. The goal is to overcome common barriers—technical issues and lack of instructor expertise—that prevent undergraduate institutions from integrating bioinformatics into life science curricula.

papers.title: Recovering anaerobic bacterial genomes in saliva, tumour and blood whole genome sequencing data from patients with prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Microbial constituents in the gastrointestinal tract, the urine and prostate tissue are being linked with clinical differences in prostate cancer, and a recent meta-analysis has linked periodontal disease to this cancer. Several hypotheses exist regarding how specific bacteria can contribute towards the development of prostate cancer. Recovering microbial genomes, and their genomic features, from clinical samples and investigating fine-scale taxonomy is a critical first step in investigating causality. Here, we describe the microbial diversity of samples associated with prostate cancer. Metage
papers.summary: This study recovered anaerobic bacterial genomes from whole genome sequencing data of saliva, tumour, and blood samples from prostate cancer patients, characterizing the microbial diversity present in these clinical samples. The work provides a resource of microbial genomes and fine-scale taxonomic profiles that could help investigate whether specific bacteria contribute to prostate cancer development, building on links between periodontal disease and the cancer.

papers.title: DNAharvester: A Nextflow Pipeline for Analysing Highly Degraded DNA from Ancient and Historical Specimens.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA (aDNA) research has advanced rapidly with the development of high-throughput sequencing, enabling genome-wide analyses of large collections of prehistoric specimens. However, analysing palaeontological and archaeological material with highly degraded DNA constitutes a major bioinformatic challenge. DNA from such samples is characterized by short fragment lengths, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and cross-species contamination, which can increase spurious mapping and reference bias, affecting downstream population genetic inferences.
papers.summary: DNAharvester is a Nextflow pipeline designed to process highly degraded DNA from ancient and historical specimens, addressing challenges like short fragments, low endogenous content, post-mortem damage, and contamination. It aims to reduce spurious mapping and reference bias, improving the reliability of downstream population genetic analyses for aDNA research.

papers.title: Evolution of lake microbial structure and function under climatic and anthropogenic forcings: Insights from sedimentary ancient DNA.
papers.abstract: Structure and function of lake microorganisms are sensitive to environmental disturbances; yet their differential responses to climatic and anthropogenic forcings over centennial scales remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed a sediment core from Lake Daihai in northern China, combining metagenomics and stable isotope analyses. Our results revealed that microbial community assembly was dominated by deterministic processes, whereas stochasticity increased notably after 1850, coinciding with the termination of the Little Ice Age and intensified human impacts. Notably, microbial community str
papers.summary: This study used sedimentary ancient DNA (metagenomics) from a Lake Daihai sediment core in northern China, combined with stable isotope analyses, to reconstruct how lake microbial community structure and function responded to climatic and human pressures over centennial timescales. Microbial community assembly was primarily governed by deterministic processes, but stochasticity increased markedly after 1850, coinciding with the end of the Little Ice Age and intensifying anthropogenic impacts. The work links long-term environmental change to shifts in microbial assembly mechanisms.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals gut segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring linked to host phenotypic maturation in Taihu geese.
papers.abstract: Taihu geese are valued for efficient utilization of fibrous feed resources and for desirable meat quality, yet how gut microbial organization varies across intestinal regions and physiological stages, and how these changes relate to host phenotype, remains unclear. We integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ITS sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and host phenotyping to characterize intestinal microbial ecology in Taihu geese at 160 days of age (D160; physiological stability stage) and 450 days of age (D450; late-laying stage). Spatial profiling of the D160 group across the duodenum, jejunum, ileum
papers.summary: This study integrated 16S rRNA, ITS, and shotgun metagenomic sequencing with host phenotyping to map how gut microbial communities differ across intestinal segments (duodenum, jejunum, ileum) and between two physiological stages (160 days, stable; 450 days, late-laying) in Taihu geese. The authors report segment-specific and age-associated restructuring of the gut microbiota that tracks with host phenotypic maturation, linking microbial organization to the birds' physiological state.

papers.title: Fast and accurate taxonomic domain assignment of short metagenomic reads using BBERT.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomes from complex environments such as soil uncover vast biodiversity. Yet most short reads produced by shotgun sequencing cannot be taxonomically or functionally annotated, as they lack a sufficiently comprehensive reference, obscuring the true structure and function of microbial communities. We introduce BBERT, a nucleotide large language model optimized for short reads. Testing on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, we found that BBERT identifies bacterial sequence syntax without relying on reference databases, enabling accurate assignment of taxonomic domain, coding potentia
papers.summary: BBERT is a nucleotide large language model trained specifically on short metagenomic reads that can assign taxonomic domain (e.g., bacterial vs. other) without relying on reference databases. Tested on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, it accurately identified bacterial sequence syntax and coding potential, addressing the problem that most short shotgun reads remain unannotated due to incomplete references.

papers.title: Beyond Taxonomy: Fungal Nutraceutical Supplementation Modifies the Functional Potential of the Gut Microbiome in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of host immune regulation, intestinal homeostasis, and recovery after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Although our previous randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial demonstrated that fungal nutraceutical supplementation with Micodigest® was associated with favorable taxonomic and systemic inflammatory changes in patients undergoing CRC surgery with curative intent, the functional consequences of this intervention remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a functional metagenomic analysis of fecal s
papers.summary: This study performed functional metagenomic analysis on fecal samples from a prior randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the fungal nutraceutical Micodigest® in colorectal cancer surgery patients. While the original trial showed favorable taxonomic and inflammatory changes, this follow-up analysis reveals that the supplementation also modifies the functional potential of the gut microbiome, moving beyond simple taxonomic shifts to show changes in microbial gene content and metabolic pathways. The work suggests that fungal nutraceuticals may influence gut microbiome function in ways relevant to CRC recovery.

papers.title: Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Recent efforts have demonstrated that systematic analysis of the millions of metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) enables groundbreaking biological discoveries. However, SRA-scale comparison of whole metagenomes has remained elusive. Here, we introduce the most comprehensive resource to date for experiment-to-experiment analysis of all SRA metagenomes, comprising FracMinHash sketches (470GB), hypergen sketches (19GB), and an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix (90GB), which we release online at https://github.com/RolandFaure/SRA-metagenome-sketches-databases . These resources enable
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors built a comprehensive resource of compact 'sketches' (FracMinHash and hypergen) for all 4.8 million metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive, along with an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix, enabling experiment-to-experiment comparison at SRA scale for the first time. This makes it feasible to search for similar metagenomes across the entire archive, supporting large-scale discovery from existing public data.

papers.title: Maternal transmission and limited virulent phage replication shape early infant gut virome maturation.
papers.abstract: Early life gut microbiome dynamics are increasingly recognized as important determinants of microbiome maturation, yet the ecological dynamics of its associated bacteriophages remain poorly resolved. Here, we performed bulk and virus like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling of longitudinal fecal samples from 32 mother-infant dyads, incorporating an exogenous phage spike in to enable absolute quantification of viral loads. Our results show that early infant gut phageome is defined by a profound lack of virulent phage genome copies while temperate phage
papers.summary: This study tracked the gut virome in 32 mother-infant pairs over time using metagenomic sequencing with an exogenous phage spike for absolute viral load quantification, plus fecal metabolomics. They found that early infant guts contain very few virulent phage genomes, with temperate phages dominating, and that maternal transmission shapes the early virome. The work suggests infant gut phage ecology is distinct from adults, with limited lytic replication during early maturation.

papers.title: Metagenomic Bioprospecting of Bioremediation-Related Genes in Amazonian Aquatic Ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Environmental monitoring of contaminated freshwater systems still lacks curated genomic resources tailored to bioremediation-oriented screening. In this study, we developed a curated catalogue of 546 genes from 80 microbial species associated with heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, detoxification and related functions and applied it to river metagenomes from four municipalities in Pará, Brazilian Amazon: Altamira, Bragança, Marabá and Paragominas. Functional annotation was performed using eggNOG-mapper and metagenomic reads were aligned against the curated catalogue with Bowtie2.
papers.summary: The authors built a curated catalogue of 546 genes from 80 microbial species linked to heavy-metal resistance, hydrocarbon degradation, and detoxification, then screened metagenomes from four rivers in the Brazilian Amazon against it. This provides a targeted resource for bioremediation-oriented monitoring of contaminated freshwater systems, which previously lacked tailored genomic references.

papers.title: Use of Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing to Investigate Respiratory Pathogens in Influenza-Negative Nasopharyngeal Swabs From Cameroon's National Influenza Surveillance.
papers.abstract: In Cameroon, national influenza surveillance identifies influenza-positive cases, but the causes of non-influenza ARIs remain poorly characterized. We applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate respiratory pathogens in influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs collected through national influenza surveillance.
papers.summary: This study applies metagenomic next-generation sequencing to influenza-negative nasopharyngeal swabs from Cameroon's national influenza surveillance system to identify non-influenza respiratory pathogens causing acute respiratory infections. It addresses a gap in understanding the etiology of non-influenza ARIs in this region, potentially informing surveillance and clinical management.

papers.title: A high-resolution spatial model of the primate gut microbiome defines niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of the gastrointestinal microbiome is shaped by strong physicochemical gradients along the gut, yet many region-associated microbial niches remain poorly resolved in humans. Here, we used the rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) as a spatially resolved primate model to profile 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract using shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and targeted bile acid metabolomics, complemented by comparative human datasets. Microbial communities exhibited strong spatial stratification along the gastrointestinal tract, while host
papers.summary: This study used the rhesus macaque as a spatially resolved primate model, profiling 148 luminal and mucosal samples across the gastrointestinal tract with shotgun metagenomics, 2bRAD-M sequencing, and targeted bile acid metabolomics. Microbial communities showed strong spatial stratification along the gut, revealing niche-specific functions and host-adapted microbial metabolism that were compared with human datasets. The work provides a high-resolution spatial map of primate gut microbiome organization and links regional niches to specific metabolic functions.

papers.title: WasteFams: a database of protein families from global wastewater microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein fa
papers.summary: WasteFams is a new database that catalogs protein families found in wastewater microbiomes worldwide, built by integrating 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (filtered to 504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes). It provides the first systematic protein-level characterization of wastewater microbiome functional diversity, yielding 3887 non-redundant protein families. This resource supports wastewater surveillance and functional microbiome research.

papers.title: Biases in high throughput sequencing methods affect microbial molecular ecology networks and keystone taxa identification in the Cinnamomum migao rhizosphere and phyllosphere.
papers.abstract: The rhizosphere and phyllosphere microbial symbiotic interactions are crucial factors affecting plant health and productivity. How to authentically reflect the species interactions and assembly processes that shape shaping microbial communities has attracted extensive attention from ecologists. The construction of most microbial networks relies on amplicon sequencing data, neglecting both total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions. The impacts of sequencing resolution ratio, microbial domain, and quantification methods on microbial interspecies interactions and network parameters st
papers.summary: This study examines how biases in high-throughput amplicon sequencing—such as resolution limits and the omission of total microbial biomass and inter-domain interactions—distort inferred microbial co-occurrence networks and keystone taxon identification in the rhizosphere and phyllosphere of Cinnamomum migao. By comparing sequencing resolutions, domains, and quantification approaches, the authors show that these methodological choices materially affect network topology and which taxa are flagged as keystones. The work cautions that ecological interpretations of plant-microbiome networks must account for sequencing and quantification biases.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: While the pulmonary microbiota may influence TB pathogenesis, direct comparisons between drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and multidrug-resistant (MDR-TB) patients remain scarce. This study explored microbiome differences between these groups.
papers.summary: This study compared the pulmonary microbiome of drug-sensitive and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients using metagenomic sequencing. It found distinct microbial community differences between the two groups, suggesting the microbiota may differ by drug resistance status. These findings highlight a potential link between the lung microbiome and TB drug resistance.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of the early gut microbiota development in Nipponia nippon.
papers.abstract: The crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) is an endangered bird whose early gut microbiota development remains poorly understood. To address this gap, this study integrated metagenomics and metabolomics to investigate the dynamic succession of gut microbiota and metabolism in naturally hatched chicks during early development.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic and metabolomic profiling to track how the gut microbiota and its metabolic output change during early development in naturally hatched crested ibis chicks, an endangered species. It provides one of the first integrated characterizations of microbial succession and metabolic shifts in this bird's early life stages. The findings offer baseline data that could inform conservation and captive-breeding strategies.

papers.title: Metagenomic and culture-dependent characterization of between-field variation in phosphorus-cycling microbial communities and functional potential across tobacco-safflower rotation fields.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms contribute to soil phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P acquisition, but P-cycling microbial communities and functional associations across tobacco-safflower rotation fields remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study combines metagenomic sequencing with culture-based isolation to characterize phosphorus-cycling microbial communities in the rhizosphere across tobacco-safflower rotation fields, focusing on how these communities and their functional potential vary between fields. The work provides a descriptive baseline of which taxa and genes are associated with phosphorus transformation in this rotation system, though the abstract does not report specific mechanistic or quantitative findings.

papers.title: Pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented transcriptional response of the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT to acidic pH.
papers.abstract: Acidic environments impose energetic constraints on ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), although some acid-tolerant lineages remain capable of ammonia oxidation at low pH. The transcriptional responses of acid-tolerant AOB to low-pH conditions remain poorly resolved. Here, we characterized the pathway-level response of Nitrosospira sp. NT by integrating a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome with comparative metatranscriptomic data from cultures incubated for 24 h at pH 5.0 or pH 8.0. Transcript abundance was not uniformly reduced among the metabolic pathways examined at pH 5.0. Genes assoc
papers.summary: The study examines how the acid-tolerant ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT responds transcriptionally to low pH (5.0 vs. 8.0) over 24 hours, using a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome and comparative metatranscriptomics. Rather than a uniform shutdown of metabolism, the pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented response, with transcript abundance not uniformly reduced across the metabolic pathways examined at pH 5.0. This provides insight into how acid-tolerant AOB sustain ammonia oxidation under acidic, energetically challenging conditions.

papers.title: Bacterial metagenome in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without OSCC by next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oral dysbiosis has been associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC); however, most microbiome studies rely on 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing, limiting species-level taxonomic resolution.
papers.summary: This study uses next-generation sequencing to profile bacterial metagenomes in dental plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), moving beyond 16S rRNA gene sequencing to achieve species-level taxonomic resolution. The work provides a multi-site characterization of oral bacterial communities associated with OSCC, addressing a key limitation of prior microbiome studies. The dataset and findings may help clarify the role of oral dysbiosis in OSCC and support future biomarker or mechanistic research.

papers.title: Baseline co-occurrence of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii is associated with greater increases in selected short-chain fatty acid-related pathways following resistant starch type 2 intervention across diverse populations.
papers.abstract: Type 2 resistant starch (RS2) can be fermented by the gut microbiota and contribute to short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production; however, microbial responses to resistant starch vary substantially across individuals and populations, and the role of baseline microbiota in this variability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated four publicly available paired metagenomic datasets representing diverse experimental and host contexts and performed cross-dataset analyses of taxonomic and functional responses. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii was among the taxa consistently enriched
papers.summary: By integrating four public paired metagenomic datasets, the authors show that individuals whose baseline gut microbiota already contains both Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii respond to type 2 resistant starch with larger increases in short-chain fatty acid–related pathways. This baseline co-occurrence pattern holds across diverse populations and experimental contexts, suggesting it could help predict who benefits most from RS2 interventions.

papers.title: Genomic insights into bacterial communities of coenocytic algae using metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.abstract: Coenocytic algae are organisms that undergo karyokinesis without cytokinesis, resulting in multinucleated cells. Most research on bacterial communities in coenocytic algae has used 16S rRNA sequencing, primarily focusing on the order Bryopsidales of green coenocytic algae. Recent studies have analyzed metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from algal hosts across multiple taxa, such as Chlorophyta, Phaeophyta, and Rhodophyta, revealing further insights into bacterial biosynthetic machinery and potential symbiotic relationships. Given the cosmopolitan distribution of coenocytic algae, such as Bryo
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to characterize bacterial communities associated with coenocytic algae, which are multinucleated organisms formed by karyokinesis without cytokinesis. Moving beyond prior 16S rRNA surveys that focused mainly on Bryopsidales green algae, the authors recover bacterial genomes across Chlorophyta, Phaeophyta, and Rhodophyta hosts, revealing biosynthetic gene clusters and potential symbiotic relationships. The work expands genomic resources for algal-associated microbiomes and highlights biosynthetic potential in these understudied communities.

papers.title: TSLC: differential abundance analysis method for identifying biologically relevant known microbes.
papers.abstract: Identifying biologically relevant microbes is a crucial task in human microbiome studies. Numerous computational and statistical methods have been proposed for this task. However, most existing methods are based solely on taxonomic information, even when whole-metagenome sequencing data are available, and thus cannot account for the fact that different microbes can perform the same or similar functions (known as functional redundancy) and for the contribution of unknown microbes to functional abundance. Hence, the identified differentially abundant microbes might not be biologically relevant t
papers.summary: The paper introduces TSLC, a differential abundance analysis method for microbiome studies that incorporates functional information from whole-metagenome sequencing rather than relying solely on taxonomic profiles. This allows the method to account for functional redundancy among microbes and the contribution of unknown microbes, aiming to identify microbes that are more biologically relevant to the phenotype. The approach addresses a key limitation of existing taxonomic-only differential abundance tools.

papers.title: Effects of cultivation of herbaceous perennials on soil microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the impacts of cultivating different herbaceous perennials on the rhizosphere microenvironment, nitrogen-cycling microbial communities, and functional genes in black soils of urban green spaces in Northeast China, thereby providing a scientific basis for rational urban plant configuration and interspecific differences in soil nutrient cycling. Focusing on five commonly utilized herbaceous perennials in Changchun (Lycopus lucidus [P-LL], Salvia japonica [P-SJ], Hemerocallis fulva [P-HF], Hosta ensata [P-HE], and Pseudolysimachion spicatum [P-PS]), this study integr
papers.summary: The study compares how five herbaceous perennial species grown in urban green spaces in Northeast China shape the rhizosphere soil microbial community and nitrogen-cycling functional genes. It finds that plant species identity influences microbial community structure and nitrogen cycling functions in black soils, supporting species-specific plant configuration for urban landscaping.

papers.title: Metagenomic profiling reveals that divergent fire-adaptive strategies drive distinct fungal succession in pine litter decomposition.
papers.abstract: Decomposing litter is a critical driver of fuel bed formation and forest fire regimes, yet how divergent plant fire-adaptive strategies influence litter chemistry and subsequent fungal decomposition dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 6-month reciprocal litterbag experiment by incubating litter from two contrasting pine species-the fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis and the fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola-in both their own native habitat and that of the other species, coupled with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession and lignocellulolytic functional profiles
papers.summary: This study used a reciprocal litterbag experiment with two pine species that have contrasting fire-adaptive strategies (fire-tolerant Pinus taiwanensis and fire-avoiding P. morrisonicola) combined with genome-resolved metagenomics to track fungal succession and lignocellulolytic functions during six months of litter decomposition. The authors show that divergent fire-adaptive strategies shape litter chemistry, which in turn drives distinct fungal community succession and decomposition trajectories. The work links plant fire adaptation to belowground fungal dynamics and fuel bed formation.

papers.title: Beyond community state types: vaginal microbial diversity and CST-IV signatures are associated with pregnancy in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.abstract: Despite significant progress in assisted reproductive technology, in vitro fertilization (IVF) pregnancy rates remain suboptimal. Although the vaginal microbiome has been implicated in IVF outcomes, prior studies often overlooked embryonic aneuploidy, a major confounder. This study aimed to investigate the association between the vaginal microbiome and pregnancy outcomes in euploid embryo transfer cycles.
papers.summary: This study examined the vaginal microbiome in IVF cycles using euploid embryos, removing aneuploidy as a confounder. It found that vaginal microbial diversity and specific CST-IV signatures were associated with pregnancy outcomes, suggesting the microbiome may influence IVF success beyond embryo chromosomal status.
